C0.quote: choosing a subset of candidates of a given size k from a set of m candidates
C0.note: Multiwinner voting rule (Chamberlin-Courant / s-Borda); computational aspects of the rule.

C1.quote: no polynomial-time algorithm can distinguish between instances with Opt
C1.note: Approximation algorithms, hardness, LP rounding; approximation guarantees against the optimal score (WD) are secondary. Core connection is a minor result.

C2.1.value: voters' ordinal rankings; preferences; preference orderings
C2.1.quote: with knowledge of voters’ ordinal rankings over all candidates

C2.2.quote: Each voter v has a bijective ranking function rv

C2.3.quote: A set V of n voters express their preferences on the candidates ordinally
C2.3.note: Preferences and cardinal utilities are mentioned, but the ranking is the only formal object.

C2.4.quote: A set V of n voters express their preferences on the candidates ordinally
C2.4.note: The ranking is described as voter preferences and the rule is applied directly to it, with no statement about reporting or submission.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.quote: the candidates are products or public projects that provide shared utility
C4.1.note: Utility and satisfaction are mentioned, and the paper uses the satisfaction version m+1-rank, but no link between utilities and rankings is defined; 'cardinal utilities' are mentioned only as something voters may not articulate.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: the maximization (or satisfaction) version of CC rule
C5.1.note: Satisfaction and proportional representation are evaluated through the Borda score, and the core connection is treated as a fairness notion.

C5.2.quote: the score of a committee is the average over the voters, of the rank
C5.2.note: Evaluated on the submitted rankings, which are called preferences, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters are only sources of rankings and take no action in the model.

ORG.note: The algorithm is a procedure, not an acting organiser.

DES.note: The designer's choice is not modelled explicitly.

C8.1.note: NA: no agent is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: provide analytic justification for using such algorithms in practice
optimizing this score implies a form of proportional representation
the core achieves a stronger notion of proportionality than 1-Borda

C9.1.note: Claims about practical use of algorithms and proportional representation of voters.

C9.2.quote: each voter on average has s “good” candidates representing her
C9.2.note: Claims about representation of voters need an assumption that submitted rankings equal voters' true preferences (not stated), and a link between rank and satisfaction (not stated).
